About this citation

Three books of essays, and the numbering is by book, so an essay reference without the book is ambiguous. Montaigne revised continually, and the 1595 edition adds material he wrote after 1588 — which means editions differ in what a given essay contains.

Exact wording

English (as recorded here)
“To philosophize is to learn how to die.”
French
“Que philosopher c'est apprendre à mourir.”

Montaigne's chapter title and thesis: to philosophize is to learn how to die. He is reframing Cicero, not inventing the claim.

Forms in circulation that differ

  • “To philosophize is to learn how to die.”
  • “To philosophise is to learn to die.”

Attribution notes

Montaigne, Essais I.20 (“Que philosopher c'est apprendre à mourir”). He explicitly credits Cicero's Tusculan Disputations for the formula; presenting it as Montaigne's original insight without that debt misstates both the chapter and the tradition it continues.

About Michel de Montaigne

Michel de Montaigne (1533–1592) invented the modern essay as a form of self-study, combining classical learning with skeptical inquiry into custom and certainty.

Interpretation

Montaigne takes an ancient philosophical claim and makes it literal. The tradition held that philosophy is preparation for death, meaning that examining one's assumptions removes the terror that makes death dominate a life. Montaigne's Essays test this against his own experience, including serious illness, so the sentence is an experiment rather than a doctrine. Learning to die, for him, means learning to stop treating mortality as an interruption.

Why it matters

Read as a reversal: we usually treat death as the event that ends a life and so put off living until it is settled. Montaigne's claim is that settling it is what frees the intervening years.

Questions readers arrive with

What is the source of the quotation “To philosophize is to learn how to die.”?

“To philosophize is to learn how to die.” comes from Essays, I.20 (1580; expanded 1588; posthumous edition 1595), attributed to Michel de Montaigne.

What does Michel de Montaigne mean by death?

Some argue that death is nothing to us; others that mortality intensifies value; still others that grief and remembrance are ethical tasks. The theme sits between metaphysics and consolation. This passage enters that discussion through death, freedom.

Is the wording of this Michel de Montaigne quotation commonly changed?

The wording recorded here is “To philosophize is to learn how to die.” Forms in circulation that differ: To philosophize is to learn how to die. / To philosophise is to learn to die. The French reads “Que philosopher c'est apprendre à mourir.”

Is this quotation attributed correctly?

Montaigne, Essais I.20 (“Que philosopher c'est apprendre à mourir”). He explicitly credits Cicero's Tusculan Disputations for the formula; presenting it as Montaigne's original insight without that debt misstates both the chapter and the tradition it continues.
